campaign: 2026-10-05: the first energy run at home (testbed/energy.md, 'First run at home' 1-2). A: the outlet map checked by load. B: the idle floors per outlet.

conditions.logger: shelly_strip.py log at 5 Hz on the laptop, over Ethernet (enp0s31f6, 192.168.100.105) to the T628L, then Wi-Fi to the strip. The strip's web UI was left open in the Claude browser pane
conditions.boards: all three booted ~13:46 by the strip's power-up (initial_state on); idle, load average ~0 at 14:19; Pis throttled=0x0; clocks synced to the laptop (Pis 14:17, Jetson 14:21 after a timesyncd restart)

conditions.measurement: AC wall power per outlet, each board including its adapter's loss; the laptop is not metered; meter readings refresh at 1 Hz per outlet (2026-10-04)

A_map_check.load_kind: timeout-bounded bash busy loops, one per core; not an LLM workload

windows.baseline: [A logger start + 5 s, first load start - 2 s]
windows.load: [load start mark + 10 s, load end mark - 2 s]
windows.clock: laptop marks (markers.tsv) against the log's sample time (wall_time + rtt_s/2)

A_map_check.rule: For each loaded board, take each board outlet's (0-2) mean apower over the load window minus its baseline mean. The map is CONFIRMED for that board if the largest rise is on its mapped outlet, is >= 0.5 W, and both other board outlets move by < 0.3 W (absolute). The router outlet (3) is reported, not scored. The map is confirmed only if all three boards pass.
A_map_check.if_not_confirmed: stop: report as found and ask the user; no energy figure is attributed to a board until the map is confirmed

B_idle_floors.window: [B logger start + 30 s, B logger start + 330 s] (300 s), nothing started on any board
computed: per outlet: mean / min / max apower and the fresh-reading rate
energy over the window by the strip's counter (aenergy.total) and by trapezoid integration of apower, and their gap, both as shelly_strip.py summarise reports them
by_minute (complete minutes inside the log) against the aenergy.total delta over the same minutes
request RTT and failures on the router's Wi-Fi
outlet 2 (AC) against the Jetson guard's 1 Hz INA3221 input-rail power (DC, module input only) over the same window
B_idle_floors.expectations_not_blind: Status reads at 13:59-14:13 already showed outlet 0 2.3-2.4 W, outlet 1 2.3 W, outlet 2 1.8-2.1 W, outlet 3 8.0 W, so these are not blind predictions: board outlets within 1.5-3.5 W, router 7-9 W; outlet 2 AC mean above the guard's DC mean (~1.25 W at 14:21).
B_idle_floors.no_decision: The counter-vs-trapezoid gap is reported as found. Which method to quote stays an open question for the user and the advisor (handoff 2026-10-04, open question 4).

not_reportable: any phase-A figure as board power under load (busy loops are not LLM work)
any energy per token (none is measured here)
